title: Local state with useState, and the derived state you should not store

videos.script:
Call a state setter, then read the variable on the next line. It still holds the old value. That surprises almost everyone once, and this lesson is about why.

{{snapshot}} State is a snapshot. Each render gets its own values, and a setter asks for a different value next time. You will press one button that calls the setter twice, and watch the week move by one.

{{updater}} Then the fix: pass the setter a function, and React hands it the latest value.

{{derived}} Next, the state you should not store. Copy a total into state, and it goes stale the moment the week changes.

{{screen}} With that settled, the planner gets its second screen. Which course is open, and the sessions themselves, move up into App, and the screens below ask for changes through functions.

{{mutate}} And last, the mistake that hides best. Change an array in place, and React does not see it. The box you ticked stays empty, while the total somewhere else quietly changes.
